transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I came in because at work, when I’m trying to explain something simple, like the inventory numbers or who’s on the weekend schedule, it starts getting all tangled. I’ll be talking about the truck delivery, and then Thursday comes into it, and then I’m thinking about the church grill we used one time—because the heat on that thing was uneven—and then my boss’s tone, the way he says my name, and people just… look at me like they don’t know where I’m going with it.

I’m not trying to confuse anybody. It just sort of jumps around when I talk.
Have you been feeling unusually high, euphoric, or irritable lately?

High, like… unusually happy? I don’t know. I wouldn’t say that. Irritable maybe sometimes, but that’s just—people ask the same question three different ways at work and then the scanner doesn’t scan right, and you’ve got the line backing up near the seasonal aisle, and it’s like, well, anybody would get short.

But euphoric, no, I don’t think so. Not like I’m walking around feeling great or anything.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t?

Seeing things… I mean, not like a movie or something standing in the room, no. Hearing things, I don’t know. Sometimes the building makes noises, the vents at work, those old vents above the break room, they sound like somebody talking if you’re tired enough.

But I don’t know if that’s what you mean. People say “hearing voices” and I think of, you know, someone calling your name from the next aisle, and half the time it’s just the intercom cutting in or somebody’s radio clipped to their belt. So… I haven’t really noticed anything like that, I guess.
Have you been needing much less sleep than usual?

Less sleep? I mean… I don’t know that it’s much less. I still go to bed, or I try to. Sometimes I’m up thinking about the next day, like whether the endcap signs got changed or if someone left the price gun in the wrong drawer again, and then you start listening to the refrigerator click on and off and it’s like counting but not really counting.

But needing less sleep, like feeling fine on hardly any? I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed that.
Do you believe anyone is trying to harm you or plot against you?

Trying to harm me? No, I don’t… I don’t think so. I mean, at work people can be sneaky about schedules, like somebody says they can’t close and then suddenly I’m moving breaks around for three departments, but that’s not the same as plotting, I guess.

Harm me, no. I haven’t really noticed anyone doing that. People are just… people get in their moods, especially around inventory or holidays. It’s not personal most of the time.
Have you been feeling like you have special powers, talents, or importance beyond what other people would believe?

Special powers? No, I don’t think so. I mean, everybody at work has something they’re good at. I can usually tell when a display’s going to block traffic before somebody knocks over the shampoo rack, but that’s just from doing it a long time.

Importance beyond other people… I don’t know. I’m a supervisor, so people do come to me for things, keys, overrides, complaints about coupons that expired two months ago. But that’s not special, that’s just the job. I wouldn’t say powers or anything like that.
Have you started using any drugs, or had any new medical illness or head injury, around the time these problems began?

Drugs? No, I mean, not that I can think of. I haven’t started anything like that. Medical illness… I don’t know, I get the usual stuff, aches, the back thing if I’m standing too long on the sales floor, but that’s been years, you know, concrete floors are terrible for people.

Head injury, no… I don’t remember hitting my head or anything around then. Unless you count bumping into stockroom shelves, which everybody does, those metal brackets stick out right at forehead level if someone leaves them wrong. But nothing serious, I don’t think.
Have you been feeling much less interested in being around other people than usual?

Less interested in people? I’m not sure. I mean, after work I’m tired, so I don’t always want to keep talking, because all day it’s customers asking where the batteries are, or someone upset about a return without a receipt, and then by the time I get home it’s like my ears need a break.

But less than usual… I don’t know. I still deal with people at work all the time. Being around people is kind of the whole job, really. Outside of that, I guess I don’t think about it much. Sometimes quiet is just quiet, you know?
Have you had a period where you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Depressed most of the day… I don’t know. I get worn down, sure. Some days after the store closes, it’s like the lights are too bright all day and then you come home and everything’s just flat, but I don’t know if that’s depressed or just being tired.

Nearly every day, though? I can’t really say. I haven’t been keeping track like that. People use that word a lot, depressed, when the truck comes late or payroll cuts hours, but I’m not sure that’s what you mean.
Have other people told you that your face or voice seems less expressive than it used to?

My face or voice? I don’t know… nobody’s said it like that to me. I mean, customers sometimes think I’m being short with them, but that’s retail, you know? If you don’t smile every second they think you’re angry, even when you’re just trying to remember the override code or where they moved the printer ink.

My voice has always been kind of plain, I think. My wife used to say I sounded like I was giving announcements over the store speaker even at home, but that was more joking, I think. So… no, I can’t say anyone’s told me I seem less expressive than before.
Has there been a time when you felt so energetic or driven that other people said you were acting unlike yourself?

So energetic or driven… I don’t know. I mean, there are busy stretches at the store where everybody’s moving fast and I probably talk more, because someone has to keep the lines from backing up, and then the scanner stops working right when there’s a coupon issue, which always happens at the worst time.

But other people saying I was acting unlike myself? I can’t really think of that. Maybe they’ve said I was wound up during inventory, but that’s not… I don’t know, that’s just the job. I’m not sure I’ve had what you’re describing.
Have you felt that other people could hear your thoughts, or that thoughts were being put into your mind?

Thoughts being… put in? I don’t know. That’s a hard one to answer.

I mean, sometimes you’re standing there at the register area and you can almost tell what somebody’s going to complain about before they say it, but that’s not them hearing my thoughts, that’s just—after enough years in retail, you know the look. Like when they’ve got the receipt folded in their hand and they’re already frowning.

As for people hearing what I’m thinking, I haven’t really noticed that. Or thoughts being put in my mind… I’m not sure what that would feel like. I have my own thoughts, I guess, even if they get crowded sometimes. But no, I can’t say that’s happened.
Have these speech and thinking problems been going on for at least 6 months?

Yeah… I think so. It’s hard to pin it down exactly, because time at the store kind of blends together — like back-to-school runs into Halloween, then the holiday displays go up before you’ve even taken down the clearance bins.

But the way people say I’m not making sense sometimes, or I stop in the middle of explaining something on the sales floor… that’s been noticeable for, I’d say, about six months now. Maybe a little more, but six months sounds about right.
At times when you were not depressed or unusually energized, were you still having these problems with your thoughts or speech?

Yeah, I think so. It wasn’t only when I was down or, you know, wound up or anything like that.

I came in because even on a regular day, when I’m just trying to explain inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, my words start going all over — like I’ll be talking about the truck delivery, then somehow I’m on Thursdays, then the church grill thing, then my boss’s tone, and people look at me like they can’t follow what I’m saying. It’s embarrassing, because I’m trying to answer a simple question and it just… jumps.
During a time when your mood felt normal, did you ever hear a voice speaking to you when no one was there?

A voice… like somebody speaking when nobody’s there? I’m not sure. I mean, sometimes in the store you hear all kinds of things — the intercom crackles, people talking two aisles over, carts squeaking — and later I’ll think someone said my name, but then it’s just the scanner beeping or somebody at customer service.

When my mood is normal, I don’t really know that I’ve had that, not in a clear way. Not like a person standing there talking to me. I’d have to think about it more, but I haven’t noticed it like that.
Have you ever had a period lasting several days when you felt unusually energetic?

I don’t know… several days energetic, like more than normal? I mean, retail can make you wired sometimes, especially when the truck comes late and everyone’s asking where the endcap signs are, and then you’ve got seasonal stuff showing up in boxes that don’t match the planogram—

But I’m not sure I’d call it unusual energy for days. I get busy, or stressed, and sometimes I keep going because somebody has to, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean.
Have you ever had a time when you felt unusually happy or euphoric?

Unusually happy… I don’t know. I mean, I’ve had good moods, sure, like when the store hits numbers or when the displays actually come together right, and everybody’s not complaining about hours or who closed wrong the night before.

But euphoric sounds like… I don’t know, like over the top? I’m not sure I’ve had that. Sometimes I’m relieved, or I get kind of upbeat if something finally goes right, but I wouldn’t say I noticed a stretch where I was just unusually happy like that.
Have there been times when you talked so fast that other people had trouble interrupting you?

Talking too fast… I don’t know. People say I talk a lot sometimes, but that’s usually because I’m trying to explain something at work and nobody’s listening until the schedule is already wrong or the stockroom’s a mess.

Trouble interrupting me? Maybe my sister says, “Hold on, let me talk,” but families say that. At the store, if I’m walking someone through markdowns or where the vendor left the pallet, I can go on because there’s a lot of details, and if you skip one thing then later it comes back on you.

But I’m not sure I’ve had a time where I was talking so fast people couldn’t interrupt me. Not that I’ve really noticed.
Have you ever felt unusually important or more capable than other people?

Unusually important… I don’t think so. I mean, at work I’m the one people come to because I’ve been there long enough to know where things are supposed to go, and sometimes I do think, well, if I don’t catch it nobody will, because the new folks don’t always read the tags right.

But more capable than other people in some big way? I don’t know. Some people are just careless, or they don’t want to learn the system, and then it falls on me. That’s not me thinking I’m special, it’s just… retail is like that. One person messes up the backroom and then three days later everyone’s blaming the supervisor.

So, no, I wouldn’t say I felt unusually important. Not like that.
Have you ever clearly seen something that other people could not see?

Clearly seen something other people couldn’t… I’m not sure. I mean, sometimes at work I’ll notice things other people miss, like a price sign turned the wrong way or someone put the seasonal stuff where grocery overflow is supposed to be, and everyone acts like it’s not there until inventory gets messed up.

But you mean like seeing a person or an object that nobody else sees? I don’t know. I can’t think of a clear time like that. Sometimes lighting in the store is bad, especially near the back doors, and you think you see movement, but then it’s just a rack or somebody’s coat hanging there. That happens to anybody, I think.

So… no, not clearly, I don’t think.

patient.answer:
Talking too fast… I don’t know. People say I talk a lot sometimes, but that’s usually because I’m trying to explain something at work and nobody’s listening until the schedule is already wrong or the stockroom’s a mess.

Trouble interrupting me? Maybe my sister says, “Hold on, let me talk,” but families say that. At the store, if I’m walking someone through markdowns or where the vendor left the pallet, I can go on because there’s a lot of details, and if you skip one thing then later it comes back on you.

But I’m not sure I’ve had a time where I was talking so fast people couldn’t interrupt me. Not that I’ve really noticed.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has ever been a distinct period of abnormally elevated self-esteem or grandiosity, to better distinguish schizophrenia from manic or schizoaffective presentations.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt unusually important or more capable than other people?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about grandiosity or inflated self-importance, which is not covered by the listed symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
Unusually important… I don’t think so. I mean, at work I’m the one people come to because I’ve been there long enough to know where things are supposed to go, and sometimes I do think, well, if I don’t catch it nobody will, because the new folks don’t always read the tags right.

But more capable than other people in some big way? I don’t know. Some people are just careless, or they don’t want to learn the system, and then it falls on me. That’s not me thinking I’m special, it’s just… retail is like that. One person messes up the backroom and then three days later everyone’s blaming the supervisor.

So, no, I wouldn’t say I felt unusually important. Not like that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there have been any clear visual hallucinations, which would support a psychotic disorder and help distinguish primary schizophrenia-spectrum illness from mood-related psychosis or uncertain nonpsychotic experiences.
doctor.question: Have you ever clearly seen something that other people could not see?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about visual hallucinations, but the provided symptom profile does not include hallucinations or perceptual disturbances.

patient.answer:
Clearly seen something other people couldn’t… I’m not sure. I mean, sometimes at work I’ll notice things other people miss, like a price sign turned the wrong way or someone put the seasonal stuff where grocery overflow is supposed to be, and everyone acts like it’s not there until inventory gets messed up.

But you mean like seeing a person or an object that nobody else sees? I don’t know. I can’t think of a clear time like that. Sometimes lighting in the store is bad, especially near the back doors, and you think you see movement, but then it’s just a rack or somebody’s coat hanging there. That happens to anybody, I think.

So… no, not clearly, I don’t think.
